punishment, as measured by suppression of response, is an exponential function of intensity of punishment, and that this relationship is independent of the species, the response system, and the method of administering punishment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
punishment is not a simple phenomenon.
punishment is an effective way to suppress behavior, and the more intense the punishment is, the greater the suppression will be.
the amount of punishment needed to reduce behavior is not constant, but varies with the intensity of the shock.
